xref.title: Missed Pan Am Flight 103 (1988)
xref.body: Matt Zvielandr, who was the number one ranked tennis player in the world at the time, was scheduled to fly to New York on Pan Am Flight 103 on December 21, 1988. For an unspecified reason, he did not board the flight, thereby avoiding the Lockerbie bombing. "Matt Zvielandr, who was then the number one ranked tennis player in the world, was supposed to fly to New York on Pan Am 103 but for some reason did not board."

xref.title: Alan Rankine Death (January 2, 2023) – Heart Disease, Age 64; Launched Snow Patrol, Belle & Sebastian, Biffy Clyro via Electric Honey Records
xref.body: Alan Rankine co-founded the Associates with Billy MacKenzie in Dundee, Scotland in 1979 — evolving out of post-punk bands and following a Bowie-like direction. A former competitive tennis player (too short at 5'8" to go professional), Rankine also worked as a production collaborator with the Cocteau Twins. After the Associates broke up, he became a lecturer at Stow College in Glasgow teaching music production, and helped students set up a record label called Electric Honey, which launched Snow Patrol, Belle & Sebastian, and Biffy Clyro. He was diagnosed with heart disease in the 2020s and died at home with family on January 2, 2023, at age 64. "He helped him set up a record label called Electric Honey, and that label launched the careers of bands like Snow Patrol, Bell and Sebastian, and Biffy Clyro."

xref.title: Historical Background
xref.body: Located in rural France, this was a French château built in 1740 on the remnants of a 16th-century structure. It featured two wings, 30 rooms, a swimming pool, a tennis court, outbuildings, and 42,000 acres of parkland. "It was an honest-to-god French château that was built in 1740 on the remains of an earlier building that dated back to sometime in the mid-16th century."

xref.title: Patrick Carney's Side Projects and Production
xref.body: Patrick Carney operates his own indie label, Audio Eagle Records, which signed the band Drummer. He also joined Drummer in the studio, playing bass, despite the band's members all being drummers from other groups. Carney's production work includes contributing to The Sheepdogs' 2012 debut record, as well as albums for Tennis and Tobias Gesso Jr. "Patrick Carney was watching an indie band called Drummer, who was signed to his audio-eagle records."
